hourly.summary: United fans are dissecting the Ten Hag transfer wreckage with the enthusiasm of a coroner — Garner, Fernandez, Carreras all discarded, Onana wanted by the Dutchman himself ('fired into the sun' per one poster), and the Mainoo dependency laid bare: 14 wins in 23 with him, zero in nine without. Carrick's already on the 'get results' clock before Chelsea.

daily.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remains catastrophically low throughout the day, stuck at a 2/10 floor with no meaningful fluctuation. The dominant themes are genuine relegation fears, a 'dead man walking' manager, the Sesko injury blow, and a coping mechanism of radioactive gallows humor — beanies as pain biomarkers, plotting to pay Rashford to leave, and treating the drop as a 'fun' alternative. The vibe hasn't shifted; it has calcified into a stable, radioactive despair where even Roy Keane on a podcast is the sole flicker of joy.

weekly.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained locked in a sustained, week-long catastrophe with scores barely moving from 2/10 across all seven days. The 4-1 Champions League thrashing by Como and a 3-0 home humiliation to Bournemouth bookended a period defined by total loss of faith in Carrick, the Glazers, and INEOS, with the mood hardening from grim resignation into open revolt — anti-ownership chants, serious relegation talk, and gallows humour as the only coping mechanism. No meaningful improvement occurred; the week ended in full-blown freefall.
